timing: Exploratory response to the measured sparsity of the two prespecified tactical probes. Folds 3/4 have already been read and are excluded entirely from this new model. Restrict all fitting, probability calibration, prediction and assessment to folds 1/2, swapping the held-out fold once. Those folds were previously used to develop the separate ordinal probes; this is cross-validated development evidence only. No fold 0 or leaderboard.
mechanism: Borrow information across training players of the same grade, so even a single tactical choice can contribute. In defense model the player's decision to extend; in offense condition on playing one atari and model whether the player chose the prespecified reference. Each role has coarse cells for the local verdict and chain size; the fine cells also specify the full-board verdict (defense) or whether the full-board winner is the reference (attack). Counts of exposures are conditioning data, not a source of direct rank evidence.
estimator: Fit rank-by-cell Bernoulli choice probabilities on unique training games (one inclusion per game, all available games for each training owner). Shrink each mean with 24 pseudo-opportunities from the label-pooled mean in that cell, smoothed by Jeffreys' half counts. For a question score each grade with a beta-binomial log likelihood per cell, fixed concentration 12, summed over cells and the two roles. Coarse correction adds alpha0 times the coarse score to the frozen SQ4 posterior logits. Full correction adds alpha1 times the fine-minus-coarse log likelihood to the coarse logits. Use the real fixed SQ4 guard afterward. An empty role with no trials supplies no evidence. No feature is estimated from another validation player's label.
calibration: Fit the two nonnegative temperatures sequentially on a 3-way stratified inner split by owner within each outer training fold. Target size/grade-balanced NLL, temperatures bounded [0,1], with both endpoints explicitly considered. Learn the rank tables again on the entire outer training fold for predicting the other fold. Fixed RNG seed 20261118, sorted owners within grade and random permutation per outer fold. A negative control destroys only the within-question-cell joint choice count by a hypergeometric seed 20261120 before applying the same fitted model; the controls retain exposure, favorable and chosen counts.
comparison: Report both outer folds' held-out guarded predictions and pooled score differences vs SQ4 and the coarse model, paired 95% intervals resampling players within true grade, equal weight to the 30 size/grade cells. A development lead requires full-minus-SQ4 >=0.001, both lower bounds positive, and improvement over SQ4 in both held-out folds. Report all outcomes regardless. A lead requires fresh data for confirmation. No tuning after the cross-validation.
